publication.heroTitle: A clearer world in three cards
publication.heroDescription: Essential science and technology news, simplified.

sections.title: People & Politics
sections.description: Important developments in governments, societies and the people shaping the world.

cards.title: Russian attack kills 30 in Ukraine's Kramatorsk, many wounded
cards.content: At least 30 people were killed and 18 others wounded in a Russian glide bomb attack on two civilian buses in the eastern Ukrainian city of Kramatorsk. The buses were carrying passengers to nearby Slovyansk which is part of a "fortress belt" that Moscow is trying to seize. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky called the attack a "horrific crime" and vowed that Ukraine would respond. Russia has not commented on the attack which is the latest in a surge of Russian attacks across Ukraine that have caused a dramatic increase in civilian casualties.

cards.title: Ukrainians Face Harsh Winter Amid Intensified Russian Attacks and Cold Weather
cards.content: Ukrainians are worried about the coming winter as Russia's attacks on cities intensify. The combination of Russian drone and missile strikes and the cold weather is making life difficult. Many people like Mariia Shostak are leaving Ukraine to find a safer place to spend the winter especially families with young children. Some people are choosing to stay in Ukraine and find ways to survive like Olena Konoplia who moved to a rural community to escape the danger and chaos of Kyiv.

cards.title: Trump Delays Iran Strikes Until After Midterm Elections
cards.content: President Donald Trump has announced that he won't attack Iran again before the midterm elections suggesting that he's aware of the war's negative impact on his party's candidates. The war has caused high gasoline and diesel prices which are a major concern for many Americans. Trump's statement comes as Democrats are gaining ground in the polls and some Republicans are worried that the war will hurt their chances in November. Trump's blockade of Iran's oil exports has reduced the country's economy but Iran has continued to obstruct oil supplies causing prices to remain high. The war has been a major issue in the campaign with many voters blaming Trump's policies for the high prices.

sections.title: Science and technology
sections.description: Discover breakthroughs in science, space, computing and emerging technology.

cards.title: Nasdaq CEO Suggests Tokenization Could Unlock Global Financial System Assets
cards.content: Nasdaq CEO Adena Friedman says tokenization could free up a lot of money tied up in assets used as collateral across the global financial system. Tokenizing assets like stocks and bonds and the flow of money could make it easier to use these assets as collateral. This could be a big deal especially for retail investors who have long wanted to trade at any time of day. To make this happen financial institutions would need to update their systems and risk management processes to work 24/7. Artificial intelligence could help with this transition.

cards.title: Federal Reserve Hints at Interest Rate Hike Before Year's End
cards.content: The Federal Reserve says it might raise interest rates again before the end of the year but didn't give a specific date. Meanwhile PepsiCo beat expectations but its profits are down due to struggles in North America. The company's CEO will talk to CNBC about its plans. Trump said he's no longer interested in a deal with Iran which caused oil prices to rise. He also signed an order allowing truckers to use off-road diesel on highways without paying federal taxes.

cards.title: Yandex Data Center Hit by Drone Strike in Western Russia
cards.content: Russian internet giant Yandex stopped working at one of its key data centers in western Russia after a drone strike. The attack caused a fire at the data center in Sasovo Ryazan and affected some of Yandex's services. The company said the data center is no longer operating and some services may be unavailable. Thankfully there were no casualties and emergency services are dealing with the aftermath.

sections.title: Health & wellness
sections.description: Medical research, public health and discoveries that affect everyday wellbeing.

cards.title: Nigerian Doctor Elected to Tackle Global Cancer Disparities
cards.content: Dr. Zainab Shinkafi-Bagudu a Nigerian paediatrician has been elected president of the Union for International Cancer Control. She's the first African to hold the role and will focus on bridging the gap in cancer care between rich and poor countries. Cancer cases and deaths are expected to rise sharply especially in poorer countries and Bagudu wants to reorient global cancer policy to address this issue. She plans to use her position to bring attention to the need for better cancer care and to mobilize resources to strengthen prevention diagnosis and treatment.

cards.title: Temperature Key to Natural Sleep Cycles, Study Suggests
cards.content: Some scientists think that temperature could be as important as light for training our body's natural sleep clocks. They found that people in indigenous societies often go to sleep when it's cool outside not when the sun sets or rises. This suggests that temperature might be a cue for sleep just like light. Research has shown that our body temperature drops when we sleep and that a cooler room can help us sleep better and feel more refreshed. Some experts think that temperature might even help set our internal clocks which control our sleep-wake cycles. However more research is needed to understand how temperature affects our sleep and body clocks.

cards.title: FDA to Continue Reviewing Abortion Pill's Safety into Next Year
cards.content: The US Food and Drug Administration says it will continue reviewing the safety of a popular abortion pill into next year. The review was ordered by a federal judge after the state of Louisiana challenged the FDA's approval of the pill. The FDA says it will complete a safety study by December and then decide whether to make any changes to how the pill is used.

sections.title: Environment
sections.description: Climate, oceans, ecosystems and the changing planet around us.

cards.title: Wildlife populations decline globally, but India sees increases in major species
cards.content: Wildlife populations worldwide have declined by 73% over the past five decades but India has seen increases in many major species according to a new report by the World Wide Fund for Nature. The report found that habitat loss and degradation are the main threats to wildlife populations but India has made progress in conservation efforts with populations of tigers rhinoceroses and other species rising.

cards.title: Maharashtra Hit by Severe Drought, 74% of State Declared Drought-Hit
cards.content: Maharashtra a state in western India has been hit by a severe drought. Almost 74% of the state around 265 talukas have been declared drought-hit after a very dry monsoon season. To manage the situation the government has ordered a 10% water cut starting October 16. Additionally the state is promoting the reuse of treated wastewater for various purposes such as gardening and industrial use.

cards.title: UN Carbon Market Body Suspend Cookstove Project Credits
cards.content: At least 130 civil society organizations are calling on the United Nations carbon market body to suspend credits linked to a cookstove project in Myanmar. The project which became the first to receive carbon credits under the Paris Agreement's new carbon market mechanism in February 2026 has raised concerns about the reliability of emissions reductions independent verification and human rights safeguards. The groups are questioning whether the project's environmental integrity can be verified citing concerns over monitoring and verification processes and are demanding an independent investigation.

sections.title: Entertainment
sections.description: Stories from film, music, sports, culture and the world of entertainment.

cards.title: Ashmolean Museum Exhibition Explores Aphrodite's Evolution into Cultural Controversy
cards.content: Aphrodite the ancient Greek goddess of love and beauty has been a source of controversy for centuries. Her nudity has been a topic of debate and her artwork has been seen as objectifying the female body. A new exhibition at Oxford's Ashmolean Museum explores the history of Aphrodite showing how she evolved into a lightning rod of cultural controversy. The goddess has two versions of her origin story a mythological one and a historically accurate one and neither particularly marks her out as a troublemaker. She was initially a goddess of fertility love and procreation but later became associated with romantic love. The exhibition also looks at how Praxiteles's sculpture of Aphrodite the Aphrodite of Knidos changed everything by showing a fully nude female figure for the first time. This artwork was revolutionary and would go on to influence art for centuries to come.

cards.title: EbonyLife Place Opens in South-West London, Celebrating African Diaspora Stories
cards.content: A new cultural centre EbonyLife Place has opened in south-west London. It's a cinema and hub that showcases black and African movies music and art. The centre was founded by Nigerian media mogul Mo Abudu who wants to celebrate and share stories from the African diaspora. It has a cinema a bar a restaurant and a boutique and will host events like masterclasses and live performances.

cards.title: The Music Man Project Honors Sir David Amess with Standing Ovation in NYC's Town Hall
cards.content: A music group for people with learning disabilities The Music Man Project recently performed in New York's Town Hall a historic venue as a tribute to the late MP Sir David Amess. The group which was founded by Amess performed in front of a full house of almost 1500 people receiving a standing ovation. This performance was a fulfillment of Amess' dream before he was murdered in 2021. The group's founder David Stanley said the performance was a testament to what people with learning disabilities can achieve with support and high expectations.

sections.title: economy
sections.description: Markets, businesses, trade and economic changes shaping the global economy.

cards.title: Trump Calls for Gas Price Relief, Offers Waivers and State Tax Cuts
cards.content: US President Donald Trump has been trying to reduce gasoline and diesel prices which have more than doubled since the US-Israel conflict with Iran began in February. He has made several announcements including a waiver on the use of red dye diesel and has called on states to cut their taxes on gasoline. Some of his moves have had a small effect in lowering prices but analysts say the only way to bring prices down is to resolve the geopolitical tensions that are causing the high prices.

cards.title: Solar Roofs Gain Momentum After Tesla's Departure
cards.content: A US company Solar Service of Colorado is handling solar roof maintenance and inspections. Some people dislike the look of solar panels but an alternative is solar roofs where tiles house solar cells looking similar to regular tiles. This is important for historic buildings where appearance changes are limited. Tesla's decision to stop offering solar roofs sent shockwaves through the industry but some see it as an opportunity for other companies like Freesuns to expand to the US. Solar roofs require collaboration among roofers solar installers and electricians and have unique challenges like repair costs and energy efficiency.

cards.title: Asos Warns of Data Breach Including Profiles and Search Histories
cards.content: Asos told its customers that hackers have detailed profiles of potentially millions of users including names addresses phone numbers emails and dates of birth. The hackers also have access to customers' search histories on the website. The company says no bank details or passwords were stolen but customers are warned about potential impersonation scams. The hackers gained access to the data by stealing an Asos employee's login credentials and using them to download the customer data.
